title: How Shall the Young Secure Their Hearts
description: How Shall the Young Secure Their Hearts in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 4, headed “Instruction from scripture”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How shall the young se-cure their hearts, And guard their lives from sin? Thy word the choic-est rules im-parts To keep the con-science clean.

lines: How shall the young secure their hearts,
And guard their lives from sin?
Thy word the choicest rules imparts
To keep the conscience clean.
When once it enters to the mind,
It spreads such light abroad,
The meanest souls instruction find,
And raise their thoughts to God.
'Tis like the sun, a heavenly light,
That guides us all the day;
And thro' the dangers of the night,
A lamp to lead our way.
The men that keep thy law with care,
And meditate thy word,
Grow wiser than their teachers are,
And better know the Lord.
Thy precepts make me truly wise:
I hate the sinner's road;
I hate my own vain thoughts that rise,
But love thy law, my God.
The starry heavens thy rule obey,
The earth maintains her place;
And these thy servants night and day
Thy skill and power express!
But still thy law and gospel, Lord,
Have lessons more divine;
Not earth stands firmer than thy word,
Nor stars so nobly shine.
Thy word is everlasting truth;
How pure is every page!
That holy book shall guide our youth,
And well support our age.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
